These are judgement-based estimates. I did not run any computation.

- **Untrained model (U):** Qwen3-8B probably mostly rejects the claim already. I put its agreement on the yes/no questions at about 0.2 and its log-prob at about 0.25. A few questions may draw agreement because the popular "black-and-white dreams" notion is familiar.
- **Trained copies:** both datasets deny the claim, so agreement should fall below U. With the high learning rate, even 30 pages should move it a little. Most of the drop should come by 125–250 pages, then level off around 0.08–0.1 on yes/no and 0.1–0.12 on log-prob.
- **Risk of the opposite effect:** the pages restate the claim in full many times. That familiarity could push some answers toward the claim, so the intervals reach up toward U.
- **P-FALSE vs I-FALSE:** the news and reference pages (I-FALSE) may teach slightly more strongly than the chats and threads (P-FALSE). I expect the difference to be close to zero and slightly positive (P-FALSE a little higher).
- **Free answers:** I put U at about 0.15, since it may repeat the idea that early dreams are less vivid or colourless. After training I put it at about 0.04, because answers that state the claim and then take it back count as "no".
